description: Housed in the historic Royal Overseas League headquarters where Scottish explorers once stayed, 100 Princes Street evokes a stylish private club for urban adventurers. Custom furnishings and handpicked antiques adorn the 30 unique, tartan-lined rooms and suites; many boast direct views of Edinburgh Castle. Enjoy local comfort fare (Aberdeen Angus burgers, lentil cottage pies) and rare Scottish whiskies in the plush dining room, The Wallace. Hotel staff provide “anything, anytime” service, while a bounty of attractions lie at your doorstep.
inTheKnow: Tailored experiences range from fly-fishing on the River Tweed to creating your own Scottish gin to curated tours for Harry Potter superfans.
summary: Setting a new standard in luxury hospitality, 100 Princes Street is poised to become a beloved destination for those seeking an exclusive, immersive and opulent Scottish experience. Located in the heart of Edinburgh, within the storied walls of what once was the headquarters of the Royal Overseas League, 100 Princes Street is an exquisitely curated haven that promises an adventure into Scotland’s rich cultural and historic legacy. Echoing the ambiance of an elite members' club, 100 Princes Street offers an exclusive escape into a world where tradition and modern luxury converge.

description: Surrounded by 185 wooded acres and steeped in French history, Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay is the chosen country escape for Paris’s well-heeled set. This medieval Cistercian abbey and former Rothschild estate now welcomes guests with 145 unique, antique-filled rooms and six distinctive dining experiences. Take a boat out on the lake, cycle around the parkland, join a masterclass, and watch movies in the private cinema. An impressive wellness spa, housed in the old stud farm, offers sound baths and aerial yoga.
inTheKnow: Every Saturday and Sunday, guests can enjoy a lavishing brunch in Le Réfectoire des Moines, which exudes an enchanting Hogwarts-inspired ambiance where constellations of candles illuminate arches.
summary: Like an immense playground in the heart of unspoilt nature, the Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay promises to make every moment a waking dream. With its attentive service to the highest degree, the enveloping intimacy of its rooms, the generosity of its communal spaces as grandiose as they are warm, and the infinite range of its activities, the estate transports us into this incredible family home 45 minutes from Paris. Over the course of the 4 seasons, by the fire or by the lake, between rejuvenation, earthly nourishment and exceptional moments, everyone writes their own Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay experience.

description: The landmark Abi d’Oru perches above a private stretch of sugar-white beach along the Gulf of Marinella. Each of the airy rooms and suites features a balcony or terrace, most with sea views; choose between contemporary and traditional décor. Lounge by the pool or indulge in a spa treatment using Sardinian honey and essential oils while the kids play in the supervised water park. Dining options include fresh seafood and Italian fare; sample the suckling pig, an island specialty.
inTheKnow: Memorable experiences range from yacht cruising and jet-skiing to rock-climbing and exploring prehistoric nuraghi. For authentic island flavor, enjoy a mountainside lunch with Orgosolo shepherds.
summary: Marinella beach, one of the most beautiful in Sardinia, lies just beyond the garden, the pool and the natural pond. Fine white sand meets a turquoise sea that shimmers through every imaginable shade of blue as it fades into the horizon. A section of the beach is reserved for guests of the Abi d’Oru and equipped with loungers and umbrellas, this is also the most sheltered area on breezy days. The new for 2026 Summer "Trattoria del Pescatore" Restaurant evokes the timeless essence of summer holidays. It offers guests everything they need to savour to the full the delights of a long day spent on the beach.

description: The 186-room Alila Shanghai transforms the city’s vibrant Jing’an district into a tranquil urban sanctuary. Its serene design—utilizing natural stone, warm timber, rattan details, and lush greenery—creates a nature-infused retreat. Enjoy cocktails on the Secret Roof terrace before dining on traditional Shanghai cuisine or grilled Japanese robatayaki. Holistic spa treatments merge modern therapies with traditional Eastern practices. This resort-style hotel sits adjacent to the historic Zhangyuan shikumen complex, and guests enjoy special access to these beautifully restored stone-gate townhouses.
inTheKnow: Slip into stillness with a complimentary gong sound bath, create your own incense or learn the ancient art of knot button-making. It’s an easy walk to Jing’an Temple and shops along West Nanjing Road.
summary: Alila Shanghai places you in the historic Jing’an district, surrounded by Shanghai’s rich history and culture and yet just a short distance from this coastal city’s modern existence as a center for business and finance. Nearby, discover ancient traditions of artisans, Shanghai Grand Theatre, museums, shopping and more. When your journeys are complete, return to your urban oasis built with comfort, luxury and sustainability in mind. Restore your body and spirit with a visit to the tranquil Spa Alila, a quiet moment in our library, a meal or tea at our restaurants, or some time at our Secret Roof bar featuring craft cocktails and outstanding views.

description: Just a mile from famed Buddhist temples lies a secret forest garden and Aman Kyoto. Surrounded by ancient woodlands that once offered refuge to a revered artist community, this secluded sanctuary pays homage to the traditional ryokan (Japanese inn), albeit in strikingly modern style. Moss-covered stone pathways wind between latticed pavilions that house 26 minimalistic rooms; healing onsen baths source their waters from nearby mineral springs. Practice yoga, take a mindfulness hike, or explore Kyoto’s 17 UNESCO World Heritage sites.
inTheKnow: Take your cultural experiences to the next level during a traditional tea with a geiko, meditation at Daiouin Temple, or practicing the art of Ikebana flower arranging.
summary: A remarkable setting, at one with the city's artistic soul Aman Kyoto represents the fruition of a beautiful landscape first conceived as the garden of a textile museum. Whimsical stone pathways curve gently along the forest floor, and stone slabs blanketed in moss serve as the foundations for the resort's architecture. The secluded grounds are part of what was an artistic community that gave rise to the revered Rinpa school of painting some 400 years ago, and are within easy reach of Kyoto’s most important sites, including the stunning golden temple, Kinkakuji.

description: Neo-Renaissance grandeur meets refined modern aesthetics at Aman Venice. You’ll feel as though you’re sleeping in a beautiful museum at this 16th-century palazzo – some of the 24 individually designed rooms and suites are covered in protected frescoes and reliefs, which are smartly complemented by contemporary furnishings and amenities. A private water transfer delivers you to the resort’s dramatic reception hall, with direct access to its private gardens (rare for this city); take the spiral staircase to the gilded dining room overlooking the Grand Canal. Meandering in a sinuous s-shape through the heart of Venice, the Grand Canal is the city’s main thoroughfare, plied by gondolas and vaporetti (water buses), lined with more than 170 gracious buildings from 200 to 700 years old. description: Experience the curative powers of Amanemu. description: Just outside Hangzhou, the “City of Heaven,” lies Amanfayun, a truly remarkable enclave where you may just find true nirvana. This blissful, secluded retreat was purposefully designed to resemble a serene Chinese village and is within walking distance of five significant Buddhist temples. No two of the 46 guest rooms, suites, and villas tucked within the scenic tea fields and forestland are identical. Many are located in original structures that date back 100 years, yet they feature the most modern amenities, including heated floors. Traditional tea in the Tea House is a must.
inTheKnow: Be sure to visit the Ling Yin temple, one of the most revered in China, and arrive in time for one of the monks’ chanting sessions. –Barbara King Leawood, Kansas
summary: Surrounded by natural beauty and history in equal measure, Amanfayun is just a 20-minute drive from the centre of Hangzhou, and a 50-minute drive from Hangzhou Airport. The airport is serviced by both domestic and international flights, and there are direct domestic flights to most major cities in China. International flights operate daily between Hangzhou and Hong Kong, Tokyo, Macau, Taipei and Seoul. There are also regular flights from Kuala Lumpur and Singapore. Access from Shanghai is either by car (approximately three hours) or by fast train (one hour and 20 minutes). Amanfayun lies hidden in a valley to the west of West Lake. description: Amangalla, set on the ramparts of Galle Fort, welcomes those who relish the chance to relive history. An easy walk through the historic fort has you taking in the old Dutch church, spice warehouses, the lighthouse, and Court Square. Return to your home base, for its palm-tree-lined swimming pool and its rejuvenating spa – therapies are customized for each guest, incorporating hydrotherapy pools, saunas, steam rooms, and plunge pools. Your bedroom is adorned with an antique four-poster bed, pettagama chest, wooden floors, freestanding bathtub, shower room, and views of the fort or the mature gardens.
inTheKnow: There’s a small alcove on the second floor where you can enjoy a drink as the sun sets over Galle Fort’s colonial rooftops. Open the windows and let Sri Lanka in! - Carrie Wallace Chicago, Illinois
summary: The stately grande dame of Galle Fort, a World Heritage Site on Sri Lanka’s south coast, Amangalla boasts all the period charm of a bygone era. Combining the Sanskrit-derived word for ‘peace’ with galla, Sinhalese for the town of Galle, the hotel stands at the junction of Church and Middle Streets with commanding views of the Fort’s ramparts. With its chandeliers and soaring fin de siècle ceilings, being welcomed into Amangalla’s Zaal, or Great Hall, is like stepping into the past. It houses the elegant Dining Room at one end and a cocktail station at the other, with a welcoming lounge area in between – ideal for enjoying a cup of Ceylon tea or an evening cocktail accompanied by live music.…

description: Amangiri (which means “peaceful mountain”) is set in Utah’s stunning canyon country and incorporates the beauty of the Four Corners desert into its design. The central pavilion, built around a dramatic swimming pool, houses the living room, gallery, library, and dining room/cellar. Amangiri’s 34 suites and 1 private four-bedroom home offer modern, airy living, dining, and sleeping areas with white-stone floors that echo the area’s natural stone; some provide private plunge pools and rooftop terraces. Be sure to experience the Aman Spa, with its water pavilion, Pilates studio, candlelit rooms, and outdoor treatment terraces.
inTheKnow: A must-do activity: climbing the Studhorse Via Ferrata (Iron Road). No previous experience is necessary, and the views are out of this world! –Chad Clark Phoenix, Arizona
summary: An otherworldly desert retreat, Amangiri is situated on 900 pristine acres in Canyon Point, Utah with sweeping views towards Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument. Located in the centre of the Grand Circle, the all-season resort, its landmark Aman Spa and its secluded camp known as Camp Sarika by Amangiri are surrounded by such iconic attractions as the Grand Canyon, Monument Valley, and Bryce and Zion National Parks. The region has been home for centuries to the native Navajo tribe and presents the raw landscape for which the American Southwest is famed. description: Everything about Amanjena is mesmerizing, including its 32 sunset-hued guest pavilions, each with a wood-burning, sunken fire pit for romantic interludes and a terrace with a cozy, cushioned seating area. The seven two-story maisons are like elegant Moroccan townhouses, each with inward-facing windows, a wall fountain, and a marble-columned bathroom – there’s even a private swimming pool and garden. Slip away to the full-service spa, with its truly Moroccan hammam and essential-oil massages; you’ll be invited to soak in a rose-petal bath and sip mint tea. Be sure to explore the numerous souks, with their countless treasures.
inTheKnow: For a memorable evening, have a romantic, private dinner in your courtyard surrounded by hundreds of candles. –Jean Pickard Atlanta, Georgia

Known in Arabic as Al Medina al-Hamra, the ‘Red City’, due to its rose-hued structures, Marrakech was the inspiration behind Amanjena’s design. The resort’s walls echo the city’s old pisé (rammed-earth) buildings as well as the Berber villages that cling to the High Atlas Mountains. description: Amanjiwo is right at home in central Java, rich in culture, spirit, and beauty. At the center of the resort is a soaring, bell-shaped rotunda, from which the guests can see the UNESCO-protected Borobudur temple. Dining facilities includes the dining room and terrace, lively bar, and Roman-influenced swimming pool. After settling into your lavish suite, with its volcanic-ash-tinted roof, handcarved furniture, and exotic Javanese fabrics, take time to explore the myriad cultural and archaeological opportunities that abound in this region. The resort can arrange excursions by car, electric bicycle, or horseback.
inTheKnow: Join the Mystical Element of Borobudur tour and watch the sun rise over temples while listening to stories from the exceptional guides. –Tisha Neufville Roswell, Georgia
summary: Amanjiwo (“peaceful soul”) is fashioned out of limestone and takes its inspiration from the surrounding culture of Central Java. The resort is located within a natural amphitheatre with the limestone Menoreh Hills rising directly behind, the Kedu Plain in front and four volcanoes – Sumbing, Sundoro, Merbabu and Merapi – gracing the horizon. Amanjiwo looks out onto Borobudur, the largest Buddhist sanctuary in the world. Amanjiwo’s suites feature terrazzo flooring, high ceilings, domed roofs and sliding glass doors that open onto a garden terrace with a view of Borobudur or surrounding farmland. Fifteen suites come with private swimming pools. All suites include a thatched-roof balé…

description: Set on a verdant hillside next to a cliff and overlooking East Bali’s Lombok Strait, Amankila is welcoming in every respect. From your freestanding suite, connected to the resort’s public areas and restaurants by stepped walkways, to the Beach Club, where water sports are available, you’ll feel at home – yet so very far removed from your workaday life. Water lovers adore the two resort outriggers, designed to emulate traditional Balinese fishing craft – cruises are offered daily. Visit two of the island’s most important temples, Lempuyang and Besakih, the former of which is considered one of Bali’s “six temples of the heavens.”
inTheKnow: Arrange for a morning snorkeling cruise aboard one of the resort’s private boats – breakfast is served on board, and there’s a plush top deck for sunbathing.
summary: Amankila (which means "peaceful hill") set on a cliffside overlooking the Lombok Strait in East Bali, offering beach and mountain resort experience in one location. Amankila’s suites are elevated to take advantage of the spectacular views to the sea and surrounding hillsides. The 31 free-standing suites, with their alang alang roof thatching, are fashioned as beach houses with a twist. All suites are connected to the reception and restaurant area by stepped walkways. description: Imagine a kingdom where “gross national happiness” is paramount, where culture and tradition hold strong, and where Buddhism has predominated since the 7th century. Amankora operates five unique lodges in complete harmony with their environment, offering an inside look at the rich culture and beauty of this stunning region. Stay at Amankora Thimphu, in a blue-pine forest; in Amankora Gangtey, overlooking a 16th-century monastery; or in Amankora Bumthang, neighbor to Wangdichholing, the palace of the first and second kings. Paro and Punakha lodges offer countless opportunities to explore the valley, visiting monasteries and temples.
inTheKnow: Be sure to book a stay at the Punakha lodge. In spring it offers a warm, subtropical contrast to your Bhutan adventure – plus it comes with an amazing infinity-edge pool. –Ally Daisa, California
summary: Amankora Paro, Amankora Punakha, Amankora Gangtey, Amankora Thimphu and Amankora Bumthang offer a unique experience of Bhutan’s impressive dzongs (fortress-monasteries), historic lhakhangs (temples) and pristine Himalayan landscapes, opening access to traditions unchanged over centuries. Sited in the picturesque Paro Valley near Balakha Village, 20 minutes from Paro’s only international airport, Amankora Paro is a 24-suite pine forest retreat commanding dramatic views of the 17th century Drukyel Dzong and the snow-clad peak of Mount Jhomolhari at an elevation of 7,300 metres. In the serene Aman Spa, guests can indulge in massages and treatments created with traditional Vietnamese ingredients, such as aromatic herbs, rice, and coffee. And in the resort’s beach club, located on a beautiful, private, white-sand beach, you can lounge, dine, swim, and enjoy a complete range of water sports, from snorkeling to kayaking.
inTheKnow: Soak in the culture and try a few popular local dishes. Don’t miss out on bánh căn (Vietnamese rice pancake) during afternoon tea at the Main restaurant and catch-of-the-day seafood in the Beach Club.

Named for the Sanskrit-derived word for ‘peace’ and noi meaning ‘place’, Amanoi is a tranquil retreat situated on a beautiful white-sand beach overlooking spectacular Vinh Hy Bay. Shaped like an elegant seahorse with its back to Laos, its tail embracing Cambodia and its belly curving into the western waters of the East Sea, Vietnam is one of Southeast Asia’s most fascinating countries. Its scenic coastline stretches in a sinuous s-shape over 3,200 kilometres from China in the north, to the Mekong Delta and beyond in the south. The original pool has been replicated amid tranquil mature grounds, and many of the Suites feature private gardens and plunge pools, adding to the introspective atmosphere. description: Amantaka is a tranquil sanctuary within easy walking distance of Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Each of the 24 suites features an airy living area with doors opening to the courtyard and a tree-shaded lounge or private swimming pool. Dine on Lao- and French-influenced cuisine in the dining room, enjoy drinks in the lounge bar, or take a casual meal on the pool terrace before visiting the town’s fabled night market. Spend days exploring Luang Prabang’s 32 beguiling temples or its many colorful boutiques, bakeries, and markets. Return to the resort’s intimate spa, sparkling pool, tennis center, gym, and yoga studio.

description: Amanwana occupies an enviable location off the coast of Sumbawa, east of Bali, and is known for its premier diving opportunities. Here, avid divers and snorkelers have access to the Sea Wall and Turtle Street, home to hawksbill and green turtles, moray eels, lobsters, and blacktip and whitetip reef sharks. (If you prefer to view your marine life from above, cruising and fishing excursions are readily available.) Luxurious tents await, each with a coral-stone deck, air conditioning, a sitting area, a king-size bed, and hardwood floors. Choose an ocean-view tent or one closer to the lush jungle.
inTheKnow: Take the river excursion that includes swimming in emerald waters under gentle waterfalls. If you're really adventurous (and physically fit), hike to the bat cave. –David Lowy, Renshaw Travel
summary: A natural paradise, Amanwana is the only resort on the beautiful island of Moyo, a veritable Eden in the Flores Sea. Overlooking the turquoise waters of Amanwana Bay – a protected marine park – this wilderness hideaway offers full-board accommodation in just 12 luxury guest tents and unparalleled access to some of the best scuba diving and snorkeling in Indonesia. There are few camps more remote than Amanwana – just 12 tents spread along the jungle shores of Moyo, a far-flung private island in the Indonesian archipelago. description: Amanyangyun is more than a resort – it is a living piece of China’s heritage. Set on the outskirts of Shanghai amid a relocated forest of thousand-year-old camphor trees, the property comprises more than a dozen Ming and Qing dynasty village buildings, reassembled stone by stone and complemented by minimalistic, contemporary spaces, all connected by paved pathways and ornamental ponds. The result is a tranquil, 24-suite retreat where time slows, allowing guests to contemplate the graceful choreography of a traditional tea ceremony or therapeutic benefits of the spa’s dual bathing rituals.
inTheKnow: The hotel’s largest reconstructed building has been transformed into a cultural center where guests can learn and practice traditional arts, such as calligraphy, or watch a kunqu opera performance.
summary: Just outside downtown Shanghai, a cherished camphor forest sets the scene for Aman's fourth destination in China: Amanyangyun. Meaning ‘nourishing cloud’, yangyun is a reference to expanding the ‘cloud’ of the mind with knowledge – a philosophy borne by the story of the trees and dwellings at Amanyangyun's heart. This introspective retreat belies a remarkable tale of a forest transported, and a history preserved.

As luxurious as the resort may be, it never forgets its roots and is in constant harmony with its island environs. To welcome the outdoors in, your pavilion features three retractable sides, as well as a king-size bed, daybeds, flat-screen television, terraces, and a sunken table surrounded by cushions for cozy dining. The Spa Villa offers a pool, deck, yoga, and Watsu spa services in the privacy of the pavilion treatment rooms.

description: The gods on Mount Olympus might well trade their celestial digs for a stay at Amanzoe. This hilltop resort, situated on the sunny Peloponnese peninsula and surrounded by olive groves, comprises 38 contemporary pavilions scattered on different levels for maximum privacy and mesmerizing views. Each freestanding structure, accessed through the central, stone-walled courtyard, features its own swimming pool and terrace with shady pergola. Guests can take advantage of the private beach club, the acclaimed Aman Spa, and a choice of restaurants; activities include sailing, waterskiing, mountain biking, and nature trekking.

description: It’s hard to beat the views at Ambiente Sedona. Each atrium (minimalist, private accommodations for two) features floor-to-ceiling bronze-tinted windows overlooking Arizona’s iconic Red Rocks. But that’s just one of the draws. This adults-only hotel also treats guests to seasonal dishes crafted with organic ingredients from the Verde Valley, bespoke spa treatments designed to ground, energize, or calm, and daily activities from Jeep tours to mixology lessons. Don’t forget your hiking boots – there’s trail access directly from the hotel.
inTheKnow: The hotel received a 2 Michelin Key award as one of the most exceptional hotel stays in the world!
summary: At Ambiente™ Sedona, our goal is to provide discerning guests seeking a scenic escape with modern, elegant accommodations in a nature-focused setting. Our landscape hotel is the first of its kind in North America. With great respect for the land and all the creatures who roam it, our innovative, elevated design provides for minimal impact to the natural environment. With a focus on the native splendor of Sedona, all Atriums are ideal for the minimalist seeking luxury in a natural setting. Lush, earth-tone palettes blanket each Atrium and floor-to-ceiling windows offer 180 degree views that bring the splendor of the national forest and red rock formations indoors.

description: Escape completely at Ilha de Bazaruto, set within a protected marine park some 24 miles off Mozambique’s mainland. Indulge in locallyinspired spa treatments, dive along protected reefs, swim with dolphins, try dune-boarding, or take a sunset cruise.

Nowhere is its beauty more pristine than the Bazaruto Archipelago, a protected marine reserve and national park. Ilha de Bazaruto, Island of the Mist, lies 30 km off the mainland. Here, rolling sand dunes melt into clear azure ocean. Swim with dolphins and experience the annual migration of humpback whales from July to September. Set sail for the sunset. Lose yourself to nature’s beauty in one of the last untouched paradises. Welcome to Anantara Bazaruto Island Resort, a truly luxury escape among Mozambique resorts.

description: Refined comfort reaches its peak at Ancora Cortina. Nestled in the heart of Italy’s fabled Dolomites, this family-owned alpine retreat features 35 cozy, contemporary hideouts with timber walls, soft textures, hand-collected art objects, and jaw-dropping views. Spend days playing on Cortina’s legendary slopes — skiing, hiking, mountain-climbing, and more — before a bespoke hammam treatment at the tri-level spa. description: If you think modern luxury (and a surprisingly fun vibe) is hard to find in a 1,200-year-old city, say hello to Andaz Prague. While the 176-room-and-suite hotel pays homage to Prague’s heritage – some rooms feature a statue of Bruncvík’s lion above the beds – it keeps things lively with vibrantly-colored furnishings, an avant-garde bistro serving innovative cuisine and whimsical cocktails, and creative workspaces for those times you need to mix business with pleasure.
inTheKnow: After exploring the landmarks in Old Town Square, head to the spa for a relaxing massage infused with Czech herbs and essential oils.
summary: Luxury lifestyle hotel Andaz Prague, housed in the iconic Sugar Palace, is located in the historical center of Prague. While wandering around the hotel, embark on a journey through the city’s stories and legends or venture out and discover one of Europe’s most beautiful metropoles. The Old Town Square is within walking distance, along with many other iconic landmarks. Let a faithful lion watch over your dreams or reach for the stars like Princess Libuše did, in the comfort of your artfully designed room.

description: Aria Hotel Budapest turns up the volume on the capital’s cool factor. Melodious sounds echo through the halls of this music-themed hotel, a reimagined neoclassical building near Saint Stephen’s Basilica. Legendary artists from Liszt to Louis Armstrong inspired the 49 rooms and suites – most offering a private balcony. Follow the keyboard tile floor (à la the film Big) to the Music Garden courtyard, with its velvet sofas and space-age piano; locals and internationals of all ages mingle in the rooftop bar for killer cocktails and views. Experience Harmony Rooftop Yoga and Harmony Spa, with its heated pool, steam, sauna, and Jacuzzi.

summary: An Experience Inspired by Music The Aria Hotel Budapest by Library Hotel Collection is a luxury boutique hotel with an exquisite design inspired by music. To compliment the musical concept, master designer Zoltan Varro's vision was to simultaneously recreate the rich, lavish atmosphere of a historic Hungarian palace while also embracing visitors in the warmth and comfort of a private residence. Aria Hotel Budapest has been awarded as the #1 Hotel in the World by TripAdvisor 2017 Travelers' Choice Awards and #1 Hotel in Central Europe by Conde Nast Traveler’s Readers’ Choice Awards in 2018. summary: Located atop the Uchisar Valley, Ariana Sustainable Luxury Lodge offers you a completely unique perspective of Cappadocia; a land that witnessed the rise of the first civilizations in world history. Cappadocia lies in the heart of Ancient Anatolia, one of the cradles of human civilization. Here, the earliest cities in world history appeared, about 5000 BC. Today, new archaeological discoveries suggest the ancient civilized cities date back to 12000 BC. Eastern Anatolia hosts some of the most important archaeological digs currently being undertaken anywhere in the world, representing a major shift in our understanding of man's early history. description: With the opening of Armendaris, you can now stay at Ted Turner’s actual home in Southern New Mexico. This 360-acre, four-guest-room property has all the luxuries you’d expect from a celebrity residence. Think private chefs and activity guides, a full Santa Fe-style kitchen, fitness and massage areas, and a gorgeous outdoor area with a gas fire pit and cascading fountain. Spend your days hiking, bison hunting, or immersing yourself in Native American history, and your nights stargazing into the vast desert skies.
inTheKnow: Learn about Turner’s wildlife conservation efforts, which help restore bighorn sheep and Bolson tortoise populations to the area.
summary: The Hacienda at Armendaris is open for reservations! The 360,000-acre property, nestled in the crimson Chihuahuan desert, embodies the essence of southern New Mexico. description: Escape the noise and crowds of Kyoto in this 52-room hilltop hotel surrounded by a verdant bamboo forest. Experience Japanese culture onsite by catching a maiko and geiko performance at the Bamboo Pavilion, or by listening to the melodies of koto and shakuhachi. Spa offerings draw from traditional Japanese healing rituals; dining spots include kaiseki options (multi-course Japanese menus); and the Bar Ryozen packs an educational punch, serving lessons in the history of rice alongside cups of local sake. When you're ready to explore, the world-famous Kiyomizu-dera Temple is just a 10-minute walk away.
inTheKnow: Take advantage of the lush surroundings by booking a morning yoga session in the property's gardens.
summary: SERENE HILLTOP SANCTUARY IN KYOTO’S GION AND HIGASHIYAMA DISTRICT Nestled on a hill beside the renowned Kiyomizu-dera Temple and embraced by a tranquil bamboo forest, Banyan Tree Higashiyama Kyoto hotel offers an intimate retreat. Stay in one of 52 luxurious rooms, each featuring contemporary Japanese accents, modern amenities and stunning views of Kyoto's historic cityscape. This hilltop Kyoto luxury hotel is the only one in the city with a Bamboo Pavilion, natural hot springs and an authentic Noh stage, where guests can enjoy classical Japanese performances. Find peace and rejuvenation away from the city's hustle and bustle at our Kyoto hotel with private onsen.

description: Set within an exclusive gated community on the Riviera Maya, the Asian-inspired Banyan Tree Mayakoba has it all. Secluded villas and suites with private pools, imaginative dining venues from tapas cruises to deep-in-the-jungle Haab-style dinners, and a championship 18-hole Greg Norman-designed golf course – the region’s first PGA Tour course. Plus, the restorative Banyan Tree Spa, with treatments ranging from Balinese massages to holistic hydrothermal therapies like the Rainforest Indulgence.

summary: Stretched along the translucent Carribbean Sea on the coast of Quintana Roo rests the multicultural and cosmopolitan Riviera Maya. Located on the eastern seaboard of the Yucatán Peninsula, the Riviera Maya extends from the town of Puerto Morelos to the village of Tulum. Mayakoba - meaning village over the water in Maya - is home to the AAA 5-Diamond awarded winning Banyan Tree Mayakoba, an extraordinary blend of Asian culture and Mexican hospitality. A breath-taking sanctuary for the senses and the perfect getaway for reflexation, rejuvenation, romance and world-class dining.

description: Heed the call of the wild at Blanket Bay, one of New Zealand's premier lodges. Take a horseback ride along the shores of Lake Wakatipu or visit local wineries. Cozy up in your sumptuous room, with its private terrace overlooking the natural splendor. Dinner, served in the lake-view Evening Dining Room or on the outdoor terrace, is complemented by your choice of the region's finest pinot noirs, rieslings, and chardonnays.
inTheKnow: In the time it takes to drive from Queenstown to Milford Sound, you can lift off by helicopter directly from Blanket Bay and fly over the Southern Alps. Dramatic and efficient! –Rachel Haile Chicago, Illinois
summary: Blanket Bayis situated just outside of Glenorchy, a small town at the northern head of Lake Wakatipu. description: Nestled in the tranquil valley of Cap Vermell, Cap Vermell Grand Hotel reflects the style of a traditional Mallorcan hilltop village with references to local art and cultural heritage. The resort immerses guests in the Balearic history; lively markets, Bronze Age ruins, the Caves of Artà, and 4 golf courses are minutes away. The 142 guest rooms offer private balconies and panoramic views. Dine at various restaurants that cater to all wishes, from modern Spanish tapas to the Mediterranean untethered cuisine of 2-Star Michelin VORO. Indulge at the Serenitas Spa with the resort’s signature treatment on the unique quartz-sand bed in Mallorca.

description: Rejuvenate your body and relax your soul at Cape of Senses. Set above the eastern shore of Lake Garda, this tranquil, adults-only hideaway features 55 suites that fan out across the hillside. Each opens to a private terrace capturing panoramic lake views, while interiors channel contemporary Italian style through clean lines and natural textures. Wild medicinal plants are used in sensory spa rituals, part of the extensive wellness offerings that include yoga, meditation, multiple saunas, and pools. The kitchen spotlights Garda’s seasonal bounty with an eye toward both tradition and innovation.
inTheKnow: Explore the region in an electric Fiat 500 or on a Vespa. Sail a boat across the lake, join a cooking class or winery tour, and enjoy a gourmet picnic in an ancient olive grove.
summary: Lightness for the soul at the 5-star spa hotel on Lake Garda in northern Italy Time and space – for yourself. Thoughts come to rest; the body is allowed to recover. A feeling of lightness suffuses you. Just watch the day go by; just enjoy being here. Where the water of the lake reflects the blue of the sky, the senses are revived. A true luxury spa resort at Lake Garda. Cape of Senses, your 5-star hotel on the natural hillside terrace above Lake Garda.

description: Capella Hanoi brings Jazz Era glamour back to the capital's Old Quarter. Housed in a landmark art nouveau building, the hotel features lavish décor embellished with theatrical memorabilia, an homage to the nearby Hanoi Opera House. The 47 themed rooms are uniquely styled; all feature wrought-iron balconies. Backstage Restaurant is a Michelin selected restaurant, and Koki, Japanese dining is Michelin Star; the only Michelin-star hotel in Vietnam. Sip bohemian cocktails in the ultra-glam Diva's Lounge and indulge in a signature moon ritual at the Auriga Spa.
inTheKnow: Discover Vietnam’s rich culture through a host of highly curated experiences. Two to consider: practicing tai chi beside Hoan Kiem Lake and a private visit to the first Vietnamese gin distillery.
summary: Capella Hanoi is dreamt up by illustrious architect, Bill Bensley, to be an Petite Auberge during Opera’s halcyon days. Just mere steps away from the iconic Hanoi Opera House, this coveted palace of revelry is, what could have been, the rendezvous spot for Opera’s greatest artists, singers, composers, stage and costume designers after the final curtain call. Within the characteristic 47-room hotel are thematic suites surprising discerning discoverers with a potpourri of original memorabilia salvaged from the glorious era, a romantic view of Hoan Kiem, epicurean choices by culinary craftsmen and curation of Daily Rituals and Programming revealing Hanoi’s treasures.

description: Located in the historic Miyagawa-chō district, Capella Kyoto bridges past and present in this UNESCO World Heritage-celebrated city. A curated collection of Japanese artworks and artifacts are on display throughout the 89-key, luxuriously serene hotel, which surrounds a courtyard with cherry blossoms and a peaceful water feature. Experience Japan’s famous bathing culture with a luxurious onsen ritual in the Auriga Spa — or in the privacy of your suite’s deep-soaking ofuro. There’s omakase-style dining at an upscale signature restaurant, along with a French brasserie and Japanese specialty restaurant.
inTheKnow: Miyagawa-chō is one Kyoto’s five kagai (geisha districts). Wander its lantern-lit streets lined with machiya (traditional wooden townhouses) and enjoy a Maiko and Geiko (Geisha) performance.
summary: Slow down your footsteps, contemplate and uncover a world of noble simplicity and quiet elegance. Located on Yamatooji-dori in the historic Miyagawa-chō district, Capella Kyoto is a reflection of the city’s ethos and a bridge between the past and present. Catch a glimpse of the elusive maiko and discover the untold stories of this long-standing tradition woven into the fabrics of the hotel. Each space tells a tale of an intimate and perfect harmony of art, culture and composition – where one complements the other. Soak in the tranquil atmosphere and relish in ichigo-ichie, one life, one moment. Four-storey high and home to 89 rooms, Capella Kyoto pays homage to the city’s rich heritage…

Concealed by the Xuhui District’s high-rises are Shanghai’s last remaining Shikumen townhouses from the 1930s, a cluster of which have been converted into 55 elegant one- to three-bedroom villas. The compound’s design has a distinctive Parisian flair and the retail space is anchored by the consecutively awarded one-Michelin-starred French restaurant.

description: A quixotic spell is cast upon you when you step into Casa Gangotena. Situated in Quito’s famed Plaza San Francisco, this exquisitely transformed 1920s mansion is the perfect base for exploring the best-preserved Spanish colonial city in all of Latin America. Its 31 light-filled rooms exude a refined elegance with towering ceilings, handpainted murals, art deco furnishings, and rich fabrics. Enjoy guest-exclusive activities, such as a visit to the San Francisco Choir and Bell Towers or a Quiteño chocolate tasting. Stop by the restaurant to sample the unique cocina mestiza concept and enjoy a house cocktail at the new Rooftop Bar.

description: Combining the privacy, autonomy, and convenience of a short-term apartment rental with the amenities and services of a hotel, Casa J.K. Spacious accommodations range from one to three bedrooms and are functionally furnished, with touches like Roman-inspired busts that lend a sense of place. Located in the heart of Rome, just steps from Via Condotti and a short stroll from Piazza di Spagna, this address represents the natural evolution of J.K.’s bespoke hospitality. Here, the freedom of a private residence meets all the services and attentions of a luxury hotel, from thoughtful daily care to world‑class amenities, allowing every guest to shape their own Roman story, embraced by a genuine sense of belonging and the timeless spirit of Dolce Vita.

description: Celebrate la dolce vita at Casa Monti Roma, an “artistic house” located in Rome’s vibrant Monti district. The 36 enchanting rooms and suites pay tribute to the Italian art of sprezzatura (effortless grace) with custom, handcrafted furnishings and colorful frescoes. Start your day with espresso and a pistachio croissant on the fountain-centered patio, linger over homemade pastas on the restaurant’s terrace, or ascend to the rooftop cocktail bar for a Monti Mirage Fizz and fabulous views over the Eternal City. The holistic spa by Susanne Kaufmann evokes the spirit of Roman baths.
inTheKnow: The Monti district blends bohemian charm with Rome's ancient treasures, such as the Trevi Fountain. Wander its cobblestone streets lined with galleries, bookstores, vintage shops and trendy boutiques.

description: The first thing to strike you about Casadelmar is how its sleek design seamlessly blends with Corsica’s natural beauty. An ultramodern marvel of red cedar and shimmering glass, the hotel has clean, crisp lines and contemporary stylings accented by bursts of fuchsia, orange, and violet. The breathtaking blues of the Mediterranean are visible from huge windows and private terraces in each of the 31 airy guest rooms and suites, and a four-bedroom villa with a pool. The views are equally stunning from the Zen-like spa and infinity-edge swimming pool, and the Michelin-starred fare pleases even the ficklest of gastronomes.
inTheKnow: Corsica boasts some of Europe’s best beaches; top among them is mile-long Palombaggia, near Porto-Vecchio. Head to the southern end to avoid the masses.
summary: On the south coast of Corsica lies the Hotel Casadelmar - a notable architectural achievement that breaks the mold with crisp lines and simple shapes. Sleek, striking, and filled with natural light. description: Bilingual Bolzano is like no other Italian city; it's only fitting that Castel Hoertenberg is unique, too. A 15th-century castle that has been owned by various barons, noble families and leaders, even serving as a refuge for the revolutionary Andreas Hofer during the Tyrolean Wars, the hotel has 24 modern Alpine rooms – many with mountain views – that feel connected to rather than overwhelmed by their history. Just like the local languages of Italian and German, the dining options here couldn't be more different: Le Meridiane is bright, casual, and breakfast-ready, while the gourmet Le Segrete is housed in the ancient vaulted cellar.

description: Time seems to stand still at the dreamy, eco-friendly escape, Castelfalfi. Surrounded by acres of vineyards, olive trees, and rolling hills, you’ll be treated to traditional Italian cuisine made with produce from the property’s organic garden, locally-inspired beauty rituals in the spa, and activities that allow you to reconnect with nature, from grape-harvesting and wine tasting to fishing, and truffle hunting. Choose from rooms, suites, villas, or apartments, each with its own personality and Tuscan charm.

summary: What dreams are made of Imagine a haven of serenity where time stands still and noise fades away to birdsong. A retreat from the world nestled in the natural beauty of Tuscany. A dreamland where you can stroll around an elegant medieval hamlet, catching glimpses of the castle as you pass enchanting stone cottages that whisper stories of long ago. A place for taking time to watch the sunrise over misty vineyards and then, come evening, gaze at the vast night sky, aperitivo in hand. Welcome to Castelfalfi, the dreamscape where time stands still.

description: The history of Normandy lives on in its chalk cliffs, D-Day beaches, and the timeless walls of Château d’Audrieu. This 18th-century manor, set amid 62 acres of parkland, traces its roots back to the 11th century. Its noble heritage endures through gilded moldings, crystal chandeliers, and heirloom antiques, blending elegance with authenticity. A meticulous renovation has elevated its charm with a Sothys spa, 29 luminous guest rooms, and a Luxury Tree House hidden among the branches. At Le Séran, Chef Samuel Gaspar showcases the flavors of Normandy through seasonal menus inspired by the château’s gardens and local producers.

description: The Château La Chenevière’s understated humility belies its 18th-century grandeur. This 29-room country house hotel, located near the Normandy landing beaches, was occupied by both Axis and Allied forces during WWII. Today, it provides a peaceful retreat where you can stroll through aromatic rose gardens or bike around the 30 acres of ancient cedars and sequoias; interiors exude a warm Gallic charm with floral wallpaper and antiques. The refined Le Botaniste serves regional dishes complemented by an impressive cellar, and the two-hectare permaculture garden provides vegetables and herbs for both this restaurant and Le Petit Jardin.
inTheKnow: The pyramid-shaped orangery is particularly stunning at night, as you watch lights reflect off the heated pool while savoring lunch or dinner from Le Petit Jardin.
summary: A former mansion and farm, this magnificent Norman chateau of the eighteenth century, “La Chenevière”, finds its charm in the testimony of the times it went through. Constructed in an area dedicated to the cultivation of hemp in the eighteenth century, then a breeding farm for exceptional foals during the nineteenth century, the chateau was occupied by the Germans during World War II, and then the Americans after the D-Day landings. It was fully restored in 1988 to become the lush hotel-restaurant that it is today. La Chenevière has now 29 spacious and comfortable rooms that reflect the elegance and romance of its design. description: Chewton Glen Hotel & Spa is just a two-hour drive from London, 90 minutes from Heathrow and 35 minutes from Southampton docks. Over the past five decades, it’s evolved from a country house into a small resort with a world-class spa and leisure facilities. The hotel has 14 Treehouse Suites and a kitchen garden that supplies much of what is served in the dining room. You can learn to cook in the hotel’s cookery school in association with the famous chef James Martin. The New Forest National Park and nearby Solent Coast provide a magical backdrop and an ideal location for pre and post cruise stays.

description: COMO Maalifushi was created for those who seek a remote, luxury escape. Guests can also enjoy yoga and holistic Asian therapies at the COMO Shambhala Retreat, with the entire guest experience defined by COMO’s exacting, passionate service.

description: A storied hideaway perched on the iconic rock in sunny St Barths. In 1950, Rémy de Haenen purchases the rocky promontory and builds a hotel upon it, gambling on the island’s potential as a dream destination. description: Experience the pampas without the pomp at Estancia la Bamba de Areco, Member of Relais & Châteaux. A long avenue lined with plane trees leads to the colonial-style building, which features 11 rooms adorned with dark woods and local artwork and textiles. Go bicycling, get a hot stone massage, or join a maté tea tasting; you can watch the gauchos display their equestrian skills or join a trail ride. After a dinner of steak and other traditional fare, relax with a glass of wine while the cowboys entertain with folkloric songs and dancing. The estancia hosts an international polo team, which regularly plays on the property’s two fields.
inTheKnow: Polo fans will love this place, as it is also home to the international polo team that bears the same name. Guests can enjoy watching their matches and practices. –Sue Lyall Hove, England
summary: Located at the end of an avenue lined with century-old plane trees, the master house at La Bamba is built around the main courtyard, with a well-endowed library in the guard tower and a panoramic gallery opening onto the park. description: Grab your gaucho garb and head to Estancia Vik José Ignacio, a 12-suite working estancia set on 4,000 acres. Estancia Vik José Ignacio is romantic and rustic, paying homage to Uruguay’s nature. Beyond its white adobe walls lies bold architectural design and funky artwork by acclaimed contemporary artists. The living room’s white sculpture and Google Earth-inspired ceiling are surreal! Spend your days playing polo or by the pool. You’ll love the colorfully chaotic, tin-walled parrilla – a barbecue room with open pit. The myriad of activities include biking, canoeing in the lake, (full-moon) horseback riding, tennis, and surfing.
inTheKnow: Horse enthusiasts will love this ranch, especially its free-spirited horses and the wide-open plains on which to ride them. –Carrie Wallace Chicago, Illinois

description: Sunlight playing off the grounds at Ferme Saint Siméon might remind you of an impressionist painting. And for good reason: Claude Monet and his fellow artists dreamed up the Honfleur School while drinking cider under these very apple trees. Today, this 17th-century Norman house offers 35 airy accommodations with oak parquet flooring, lush fabrics, and fine furnishings; many overlook the Seine estuary (some of them will propose steam shower and balneo bathtub after refurbishment). The Bistro La Boucane, in the "chaumière of Monet,” and the gastronomic restaurant welcomes you. Enjoy local, seasonal produce by executive chef Matthieu Pouleur.
inTheKnow: Take a painting lesson with the resident artist in the hotel’s rose gardens and sit where Monet captured the same landscape on canvas.
summary: Ferme Saint Simeonis a beautiful 17th century Norman house located on the heights of Honfleur, boasting a panoramic Seine Estuary view, whose lights fascinated the masters of impressionism. Location The historical center of Honfleur is only a few minutes walk from the hotel';s peaceful gardens. Only 2 hours drive from Paris. description: It's the little touches you'll remember most about Four Seasons Resort and Residences Jackson Hole – warm ski boots brought to you before you hit the slopes, that memorable fly-fishing trip, or the in-room massage after a day of hiking. description: An oceanfront estate held sacred by Hawaiians adjoins the 370-room Four Seasons Resort Oahu at Ko Olina. The celestial setting makes for an idyllic escape from Oahu’s more touristy scene; here, guests can stroll their own beach and snorkel with sea turtles. Practice sunrise yoga, try stand-up paddleboarding, and enjoy preferred tee times at the Ko Olina Golf Club; deep-sea fishing and whale-watching are available at the Ko Olina marina. There are plenty of activities for the kids, along with quiet relaxation by the adults-only pool. Dining ranges from fresh seafood at Mina’s Fish House to Italian favorites at Noe.

summary: On Oahu’s sunny western coast – wild, rugged and conveniently close to Honolulu and Waikiki Beach – five-star Four Seasons Resort Oahu at Ko Olina balances a classic Hawaiian style with one-of-a-kind luxury. Chic and light-filled with vast ocean views, our 371 accommodations provide a personal sanctuary in this all-encompassing Hawaiian luxury beach resort. Restaurants and bars are infused with the magnetic energy of Ko Olina. Splash into lively pools and lagoons, with numerous water sports right off the Resort’s own beach. Play tennis and golf, then relax in the Spa – wrapped in the effortless elegance of Four Seasons.

description: Tucked away in Edinburgh’s bustling St. Andrew’s Square, you’ll find the grand yet intimate Gleneagles Townhouse – a 33-guestroom property with a discreet entrance and glamorous neo-Victorian vibe. Rooms embrace the building’s noble heritage with high ceilings, antique rugs, and free-standing tubs. The all-day restaurant serves international dishes like west coast langoustines and pumpkin and feta tarts. Timeless charm blends with all today’s needs in our boutique hotel bedrooms. Deeply comfortable, they’re sanctuaries of downtime as the city sleeps. Great dining and sipping are best savoured in good company. Our all-day restaurant and bar, open to all, is a place for great get-togethers and happy huddles. Our rooftop bar serves classic cocktails and vast views. And private dining is tucked away; as it should be. Gleneagles Townhouse is a place to gather and be glorious.

description: Find inspiration at Grand Hotel Portovenere. This converted 16th-century Franciscan monastery sits at the direct point where the UNESCO-designated Cinque Terre meets the celebrated Gulf of Poets. Simple, modern decor and a soft palette create a soothing ambience in the 46 rooms; the higher the floor, the better the pinch-me views over the sea and Palmaria Island. Soak it all in over Rossinis on the Venus Bar’s veranda or contemporary regional fare in the restaurant. You can join the chef for a pesto-making class, visit oyster farms in La Spezia, or delve into the area’s viticulture.

description: Follow in the footsteps of Audrey Hepburn and Sophia Loren and experience the glamour, romance, and luxe way of life at Grand Hotel Timeo. Located beside an ancient Greek theater, its 70 guest rooms are decorated in exquisite Italian baroque, and most boast views of the sea and Mount Etna. Stroll through town to shop for ceramics and visit local artisans, then visit the hotel's Wellness Centre, set within the verdant park, for a spa treatment made with local flowers and fruit essences. Dinner on the terrace overlooking majestic Mount Etna features tantalizing Sicilian and Mediterranean cuisine.

summary: Grand Hotel Timeo is now open and will close on the 29th of November, 2026. Grand Hotel Timeo, a Belmond Hotel, is a storied hideaway in the heart of Taormina. Set high on rugged cliffs, next to the magnificent Greek Theatre, its views span majestic Mount Etna and shimmering Naxos Bay. Since the mid-1800s, this tranquil enclave has proved irresistible to celebrated writers and Hollywood icons alike. Its famed Literary Terrace has welcomed Oscar Wilde, DH Lawrence and Truman Capote, as well as dolce vita icons Cary Grant and Audrey Hepburn. description: Those seeking sun, solitude, and serious farm-to-table Caribbean cuisine will feel right at home at Guana Island. Spread out over 850 acres of pristine natural beauty, this all-inclusive hideaway has it all: whitewashed cottages and villas with private entrances and ocean views, a restaurant built into an eighteenth-century ruin serving Michelin-worthy local and international specialties, and seven secluded beaches to soak in those laid-back island vibes. inTheKnow: Ever dreamed of having an island all to yourself? You can rent the entire 18-room resort and customize every detail of your stay, including what’s on the menu.
summary: Imagine the Caribbean before it went public… One of the few private islands in its part of the world, Guana remains the most unspoiled jewel of the British Virgin Islands. Our 850 acres, seven beaches, mountains, gardens, organic orchard, dozens of hiking trails, and even our flock of flamingos are the exclusive domain of a handful of guests for the duration of their stay. There is no public bar, marina, or any other commercial facility on the Island. Guana’s understated elegance and absolute privacy (only registered guests are permitted) have made it a hideaway retreat for a century’s worth of luminaries from the worlds of art, literature, politics, and industry.

description: Time seems to stand still at Halekulani Okinawa. Perched on the city’s central coast, the hotel boasts 360 open and airy rooms and suites, all of which feature a private balcony and Halekulani’s signature “Seven Shades of White” color scheme. There are also four distinct restaurants, including Shiroux, helmed by Michelin-starred chef Ken Sakamoto, five pools (the Orchid Pool’s mosaic tiles are a must-see), and a spa offering ancient healing remedies infused with traditional ingredients to promote an even greater sense of calm.
inTheKnow: For the ultimate sanctuary, stay in one of the hotel’s five villas, complete with a private heated pool and a natural hot spring-fed bath.
summary: Halekulani brings understated, timeless elegance to a setting of breathtaking natural beauty in Okinawa. Guests are invited to explore and discover the soul of these islands in luxurious comfort and seclusion, while experiencing the legendary service for which the Halekulani name is known. Halekulani, from the Hawaiian for ‘House of Befitting Heaven’, has a century-long history on Waikiki Beach, Hawaii in the United States. Born from the legacy built over generations, Halekulani Okinawa brings a new era of luxury to the beautiful coastal waters of the Okinawa Kaigan Quasi-National Park in Onna Village, Okinawa.

Far from everything and yet close by, the endless vastness provides privacy, harmony and security. Seclusion combined with exclusivity that meets the needs of families, groups of friends, couples and individuals.

description: In the historic heart of Córdoba, Hospes Palacio del Bailío is a historical palace, dating back to the sixteenth century. description: Expect to be awed at Hotel AWA, an all-inclusive retreat at the gateway to Northern Patagonia. Perched above Lake Llanquihue with breathtaking views of the Osorno Volcano, Chile’s first B Corp hotel is a modern stunner with a focus on sustainability, adventure, and cultural heritage. Local textiles and artworks adorn the 25 minimalist, glass-walled rooms and suites, while the restaurant fuses German and Creole flavors with ingredients from the organic, regenerative garden. Inspired activities range from guided hikes to helicopter flightseeing.
inTheKnow: Go rafting along the Petrohué River, discover the local traditions of basketry and loom weaving, or spend a day soaking in the Termas del Sol hot springs.
summary: Hotel AWA is an independent family project focused on offering excellent lodging, dining, and spa services. Every guest’s stay is made to measure, even before their arrival. The All-Included program includes a private guide, who helps create the most memorable experiences. We focus on delivering personalized service with great attention to detail. AWA is located at the entrance to Patagonia, surrounded by national parks and volcanoes on the banks of the large Lake Llanquihue and less than an hour from the Puerto Montt airport. We are the starting point for exploring Patagonia.

Plus, chic brasseries and cozy bars that radiate Belle Epoque charm. There’s also the renowned Diane Barrière Spa to help you get red carpet ready, whether you’re going out on the town or attending the American Film Festival, held each year in September.

Dive into the private pool, daydream on the Planches boardwalk, place a bet at the Casino and visit the American Film Festival. Deauville is at your door.

description: With its rich history and its unique location in the city centre, the Bayerischer Hof is one of Munich's most legendary hotels. From the moment you step through its grand entrance, you're transported into a world of refined charm and timeless sophistication. Each corner of the hotel tells a story — from opulent rooms adorned with classic and modern design, to panoramic rooftop views at the Blue Spa or our breakfast in the Dachgarten.

summary: The journey continues through five exceptional restaurants, including our two michelin starred Atelier, where culinary artistry meets global flavors. description: Wondering what would be an ideal day during your stay at Hotel de Toiras? Start your morning with a full breakfast with homemade jams and local produce in the Salon d’Olivia. Pick-up your bicycle at the entrance of Hotel de Toiras and roam around the beautiful villages of the island of Ré, salt marshes and vineyards. Feeling hungry? Stop right at an oyster hut to enjoy the best oysters with locally produced white wine and ocean-front scenery. Drop off your bicycle and stroll in the local market. Time to return to the hotel to sip a cocktail in our terrace bar overlooking the harbor and memorable sunset.

The facade, typical of the old Île de Ré residences, subjected to the forces of the Atlantic Ocean for nearly four centuries, makes the hotel an integral part of this harbor town and endow it with great natural charm. The main patio area is decadently loungy, full of orchids and plants; another offers alfresco dining, while the signature restaurant fronts the Daule River. summary: In the old Nice, nestled in the North-Italian part of Provence, lies a convent from the 17th century with a luxurious garden. A picture of light and simplicity. At the Hôtel du Couvent, time is passed by reading in the shade of a fig tree, indulging in a few strokes in the lap pool or chatting with the next table at the guinguette cafe. You can take time to meditate at the Movement Studio, seek advice at the herbalist in the cloister or enjoy a thermal treatment at the Roman baths, before stepping out into the hustle and bustle of the centre of Nice.

description: Located in the vibrant Itaim-Bibi neighborhood, Hotel Fasano Sao Paulo Itaim spans 20 floors and an array of luxurious styles that create a warm, sophisticated ambiance. Get a body sculpting spa treatment before lounging by the rooftop pool; the adjoining bar is a trendy spot for sundown cocktails overlooking the sprawling cityscape.

The hotel also opens the second location of Gero restaurant in São Paulo.

description: Owned and managed by Roberto B. Jr. and Veruschka Wirth, who represent the sixth generation of a famous Swiss hotelier family, Hotel Hassler Roma stands at the top of the Spanish Steps as the epitome of “la dolce vita.” In the hotel’s 82 elegantly appointed guest rooms and suites, you’ll find walk-in closets and classic or contemporary decor. Hotel Hassler: where tradition meets innovation in the heart of Rome. Choose us for elegance, comfort, and unparalleled service in the Eternal City.

description: Expect a most enchanted stay at Hotel Solar de las Ánimas. description: Walking amid the hills that surround Inkaterra Hacienda Urubamba is to tread upon one of the most fertile lands in the Americas. description: InterContinental Hua Hin Resort channels 1920s Thai royal heritage with a colonial-era elegance updated for modern comfort. With stunning cultural attractions and temples, world-class golf courses and hillside vineyards, Hua Hin continues to charm visitors and ensure memorable holiday experiences.

description: Inspired by ancient Javanese-Hindu water palaces, Jumeirah Bali is designed to soothe the senses. Its clifftop perch along the island’s southern coast provides sweeping Indian Ocean views; lush jungle and gardens surround the 123 airy villas, each boasting its own plunge pool and butler service. Practice yoga, surf beautiful Dreamland Beach, or play a round at the adjacent New Kuta Golf Course, then relax in Bali’s only Turkish hammam. Flame-grilled cuisine gets an Asian twist at the cliffside Akasa restaurant.

description: Far from Edinburgh’s crowded streets (and overlooking the city’s most beautiful private garden squares) is Kimpton Charlotte Square Hotel. Comprised of seven interconnected Georgian townhouses, the newly renovated hotel employs rich woods, plush fabrics, and pops of color – including a smart use of tartan plaid to create a sophisticated, yet comfortable appeal. For smaller group travel, enjoy the exclusivity of the No.33 Townhouse - a 12 guest room Georgian Townhouse.
inTheKnow: Eat the seasons at AIZLE at Kimpton Charlotte Square and find out why this is Edinburgh's number 1 fine dining restaurant on Tripadvisor. Enjoy 6 course menu tastings with wine pairings.
summary: Perched on the edge of a picturesque private garden in the New Town, Kimpton Charlotte Square Hotel blends traditional glamour with the Scotland of today. Outside, a classical Georgian exterior stands as an ode to the past while inside, past the lobby, a glass-topped central courtyard is abuzz with activity as travellers unwind over gin & tonics, local professionals do business, and friends toast special occasions. The energy is so fresh and effervescent that you’ll want to bottle it and bring it home—but then again, it feels too distinctly Edinburgh to make sense anywhere else.

It gets even better as our hotel is located in Bangkok’s city centre, where the city’s top attractions are only a stone’s throw away. Trust us, you won’t find a better second home after you’ve discovered the Kimpton Maa-Lai Bangkok experience.

description: Contemporary and playful in design, and yet surrounded by lush rain-forest canopy, Kurà is a dynamic concept fusing sustainability and natural beauty. Lounge in a two-person hammock on the veranda or swim into the sunset in the stunning infinity-edge pool. description: L’AND Vineyards makes a modern minimalist statement in Portugal’s renowned Alentejo wine region. description: Fans of Tuscany, look no farther: Maremma is your place. Here, rolling hills with vineyards and olive groves meet the white-sand beaches and clear blue waters of the Mediterranean coast. Once the residence of the duke of Tuscany, today L'Andana is a one-of-a-kind resort set on a 1,250-acre estate. The hotel's bedrooms and suites overlook vineyards and olive groves. A one-Michelin-starred chef looks after the dining experience, starting with a lavish breakfast. Other pleasures include a tennis court, a driving range, a pampering ESPA, and a peaceful swimming pool. However, it may be the Italian cooking courses that strike your fancy.
inTheKnow: L'Andana ESPA signature treatments make use of such local ingredients as estate-grown herbs and extra-virgin olive oil.

The cities of Florence, Siena, Pisa as well as many other major historical, archaeological and cultural sites are in the vicinity. The hotel is located on the 500-hectare estate of Tenuta La Badiola. description: Lying just across from the Popes’ Palace, La Mirande has gone through many incarnations. Ruins from the original 14th-century cardinal’s residence were used in restoring the baroque mansion, now reborn as a 26-room hotel in the style of the Age of Enlightenment. You’ll be fascinated by the rich tapestries, indienne fabrics, silk-lined curtains, vintage wallpapers, and Carrara marble, as well as modern touches, such as in-mirror televisions. Take a nightly gastronomic journey in the coffered-ceilinged restaurant; cooking classes teach Provençal secrets with copper pots over the kitchen’s wood-burning stove.

summary: Set in an old mansion at the foot of the Palais des Papes in the heart of Avignon, La Mirande is steeped in secular history. The hotel is named after the famous room in the Palais des Papes, where the Pope’s representatives held receptions for the city’s notables and visiting high-ranking officials. Originally a Cardinal’s Palace in the 14th century, the ruins of La Mirande were restored during the 17th century to create the Hôtel de Vervins and its baroque façade by architect Pierre Mignard, later becoming the Hôtel Pamard between the late 18th and 20th centuries. description: La Zambra Resort brings fresh energy to the Mijas Costa. The legendary Byblos Hotel has been totally reimagined as this 196-room retreat showcasing modern Andalusian design, while the Robert Trent Jones–designed golf course sweeps across the rolling landscape. Stroll the shaded pathways, lounge by your choice of pools, indulge in a curated wellness treatment at the region’s largest spa, and savor a gastronomic journey around Andalusia at five unique dining venues. La Zambra makes an ideal base for exploring the white village of Mijas, Alhambra Palace in Granada, and other nearby attractions.

summary: Originally opened in 1986 as the iconic Byblos Hotel, this landmark in the hills of Mijas became one of the Costa del Sol’s most prestigious addresses, renowned for its discretion, elegance, and appeal to international jet-setters and royalty. description: Dominate the slopes at the 55-room Le Coucou in Méribel. Enjoying unrivalled access to the Trois Vallees, this ski-in/ski-out hotel combines the elegance of a traditional chalet with a playful, contemporary aesthetic that feels cozy and comfortable. You’ll find all the usual powdery play and then some — including paragliding, electric fat bikes, and a double zip-line. Restore tired muscles in the spa before dining on Wagyu Bolognese at the upscale Beefbar steakhouse or cheese fondue in the rustic Le Fumoir.

summary: In the heights of Belvédère, at an altitude of 1,600m at the foot of the Rond-Point des pistes, right on the edge of the slopes, Le Coucou is quite simply the most beautiful nest in Méribel. Up there, the hotel looks down on the snow-covered peaks and dominates the entire valley. Part of the Maisons Pariente hotel collection, Le Coucou opens its doors from December to early April every year. Nestled in a charming wooden chalet like the mischievous bird from which it takes its name, Le Coucou interprets the art of chic, relaxed mountain living. 5-star luxury is sublimated in every experience, thanks to the attentive service of our teams. description: Set on a secluded beach on Sardinia's Costa Verde — a wilder contrast to the ritzy Costa Smeralda — Le Dune Piscinas is a remote hideaway spotlighting all that makes Sardinia special. Surrounded by UNESCO-certified sand dunes known as Italy's "Little Sahara," Mediterranean scrub, and Sardinian deer in the distance, the 28-room hotel is a prime retreat, but was once an industrial space as the terminus of a mining railway. Today, the focus is on wellness and island living, with a spa overlooking the dunes and dining that centers on Sardinian ingredients and flavors.

description: A 19th-century villa turned Art Deco resort, Les Roches Blanches has transformed once again into a retro-chic seaside hideaway. The 45-room hotel lies between the village of Cassis and its Calanques, directly facing Cap Canaille; terraced gardens, shaded by umbrella pines, lead past two pools to a sea access. This peaceful haven created by Alice and Jerome Tourbier is the ideal place to relax, unwind and enjoy the good things in life. It is a homely place where you’ll feel good, an experience in the great outdoors, with some of the greatest vintage wines and gourmet delights, to help you completely let go and revitalize. Welcome to Les Sources de Cheverny!

description: Deriving its name from the Sanskrit word for “temple,” Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve stands as a tropical shrine dedicated to the self. Fronting the Ayung River near the Ubud jungle, the hotel – which features 35 suites and 25 private pool villas, each with its own butler – replicates a traditional Balinese village, complete with working rice paddies. Four restaurants serve health-conscious cuisine sourced from the organic garden; arrange to have a romantic dinner overlooking the river or rice terrace. The spa offers a variety of programs focused on physical and spiritual well-being.

summary: Ubud’s magic not only lies in its charm and centuries old spiritual and cultural richness. The discovery of hidden temples, the view from atop an active volcano or bonds re-built on the mighty Ayung River rafts are some of inspiring and memorable team building activities at Mandapa. For thousands of years, the mandapas, Sanskrit for temples, of Ubud have offered a sacred space for devotees to rest their mind, body and soul. Visitors today will find a similar escape at Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve; a secluded paradise where lush, rolling hills, the Ayung River and verdant rice paddies create a unique sense of place. description: Mandarin Oriental, Vienna brings the brand's signature Asian stylings to the "Capital of Music." Housed in a landmark Art Nouveau building within the UNESCO-listed Ringstrasse — steps from St. Stephen's Cathedral and the State Opera House — this elegantly refined hotel lures with 138 soothing, thoughtfully appointed rooms and suites bathed in natural light. The sophisticated, seafood-focused Le Sept and a convivial, all-day brasserie are among four distinct culinary venues. You'll find the city's largest swimming pool and healing, Eastern-influenced therapies in the subterranean spa.
inTheKnow: Ask the concierge about exclusive Opera House access, an after-hours tour of the MAK (Museum of Applied Arts), or a private ride on Vienna's iconic Ferris Wheel.
summary: A historic hotel with contemporary touches, Mandarin Oriental, Vienna offers five-star luxury in the picturesque Old Town, just steps from the city's top attractions. Experience four different culinary destinations in Vienna, where Art Nouveau elegance meets authentic cuisine and cultural heritage blends with refined dining. Our serene spa sanctuary invites you on a journey of complete rejuvenation and renewal. Inspired by Vienna’s unique blend of art, culture, and nature, our tailored treatments and exclusive wellness facilities offer a truly holistic experience for body and mind.

The wellness hub focuses on individualized, self-care rituals that might include yoga al fresco, hammam treatments, and floating in the heated cave pool. MANNA is open all year round and welcomes guests above 11 years old.

description: Name #1 Best Restort Hotel in Canada by Travel + Leisure. Established in 1899, this five-star family-owned Relais & Châteaux estate is nestled in 35 acres of beautifully landscaped gardens and birch forest along the shores of Lake Massawippi in North Hatley, Québec. The retreat offers 32 luxury rooms, 84 suites, 14 Andalusian-style villas, and the grand Villa del Mar, set in 45,208 square feet of subtropical gardens. description: Escape the cookie-cutter Miami hotel template at Mayfair House Hotel & Garden, which is full of whimsy and local flair. summary: Mayfair House Hotel & Garden, an icon of Coconut Grove that first opened in 1985, reopened September 2022. Honoring the neighborhood’s inherent artistic spirit, no two rooms at the Mayfair House Hotel & Garden are exactly alike, promising guests a new experience each time they visit.

description: Monasterio, a 1592 monastery turned into a luxury hotel in Cusco, makes it possible for guests to learn about Spanish and Inca cultures during their stay. Enjoy an Andean massage based on a ritual developed by Andes natives; an aromatherapy treatment is administered using qantu, the sacred flower of the Inca. Visit the Lobby Bar for a wide selection of cocktails made from original recipes, and then dine on Peruvian and international dishes at El Tupay restaurant. Take time to meditate on your sacred destination in your Spanish Colonial-Style bedroom, where religious art and local décor adorn the walls.
inTheKnow: Dine outside in the gorgeous courtyard by the ancient fountain if the weather allows; ask for a tour of the hotel if time allows. –Eleanor Hardy Louisville, Kentucky
summary: Looking out of the window at Monasterio, a Belmond Hotel in Cusco, hearts may soar as high as the Andean mountains. The stirring views, together with an authentic immersion in Peruvian culture, make a stay here truly uplifting. Just steps from Cusco’s lively central square, the hotel is set in a restored 16th-century monastery built on the foundations of an Inca palace. From the outside, whitewashed stone walls give little hint as to the splendid interiors within. Guests enter to discover graceful archways, cobbled paths and a cloistered courtyard complete with scented flowerbeds, a fountain and a 300-year-old cedar tree. It’s blissfully tranquil here and Cusco’s altitude is easily managed.…

Neo-Renaissance and distinctly New York, the hotel has several locally beloved meeting spots: the bistro-style Corner Bar, the refined Dining Room, and the opulent martini spot Swan Room, set in the former bank teller area.

description: Every tatami mat, shoji screen, and lavish kaiseki dinner reveals a peek inside Nishimuraya Honkan’s 160-year history. The ryokan (Japanese-style inn) traditional architecture transports you into another era – one with lush gardens, indoor and outdoor hot springs, and artfully-crafted multi-course meals featuring Matsuba crab (winter only), Tajima beef, and Konotori rice served in the privacy of your room. Don’t miss the two-level museum showcasing an expansive collection of local photos, paintings, and relics.
inTheKnow: Guests receive complimentary access to all of Kinosaki’s public onsens, several of which are within a 5-15-minute walk.
summary: Nishimuraya Honkan is part of Virtuoso’s exclusive Regional Program for Asia. The gardens of Nishimuraya Honkan allow guests to experience the kaleidoscope of variation that Japans four seasons bring. Guest rooms were designed with as much thought given to the outside as the inside. Whether it is the elegant cherry blossoms of spring, the gentle breezes off the Sea of Japan in the summer, the colorful leaves of autmun, or the delicate snows of winter, you are sure to discover a wealth of natural beauty in Kinosaki Onsen.

description: Heat things up at Octant Furnas, a 55-room, eco-conscious retreat located on the Azores’ largest island. description: With its bucolic setting and boho-chic vibe, Vila Monte gives “down on the farm” a decidedly fashionable edge. Shades of white soothe tired souls in the 55 rooms adorned with tree-trunk coffee tables and handcarved accents. description: Orient Express Venezia occupies a 15th-century noble residence that once lodged the Duke of Urbino. The 45 elegantly detailed rooms and suites overlook gardens and the canals. Sip a Venetian spritz in the bar before dining on fine Italian fare in the outstanding restaurant.

summary: A 15th-century Venetian palace reawakens after an eight-year renovation by architect Aline Asmar d’Amman. The Palace was transformed in the 1800s by architect Gian Battista Meduna and beautified with layers of Neo-Gothic and Baroque splendor. Once home to the Duke of Urbino and the Donà and Giovannelli families, it later became a Pinacoteca. Now, through Orient Express, it begins a new hospitality chapter, honoring the legacy of a noble mansion while embracing the spirit of the iconic hotel brand. Just ten minutes from the historic quay, the palace gleams anew, its courtyard, terraces, and garden inviting exploration.

description: Experience Lisbon’s history and cultural heritage while staying at the 61-room Palacio Ludovice Wine Experience Hotel. Occupying an entire block in the central Bairro Alto neighborhood — and boasting the same scenic views as the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara — this 18th-century palacete incorporates Azulejo tiles, frescoes, and other original elements in its contemporary design. Join daily wine tastings, indulge in a Vinothérapie spa ritual, and admire the courtyard’s vertical garden while dining on reimagined Portuguese classics at Federico restaurant.
inTheKnow: Explore the nearby Moorish Quarter before sampling fine ports at the wine bar’s dramatic, floor-to-ceiling counter. Note the brick ceiling —a remnant of its wine cellar days.
summary: Located in the heart of Lisbon amidst the mythical Chiado, Bairro Alto and Príncipe Real neighbourhoods, facing the breathtaking panoramic views of the São Pedro de Alcântara Viewpoint. Former private residence of João Federico Ludovice, architect to King João V in the 18th century, its rooms and halls are brought back to life as 61 rooms and suites, completely transformed under the eye of the architect Miguel Câncio Martins to bring to life the ultimate luxury boutique hotel experience in the city.

description: Tucked away behind the Ringstrasse and overlooking the Stadtpark, Palais Coburg remains one of Vienna’s most private and distinctive addresses. Following an extensive renovation and reopening in 2026, the palace combines historic architecture with contemporary interiors while preserving the character of the building itself. The 36 redesigned suites are spacious, individually styled and intentionally residential in feel.
